description:
FOUND s492a (Opus, 2026-09-20) as the residue of #1999: with the `$)` lex
repair and the `use builtin` import, core File::Copy LOADS and
copy/cp/move all work (7 of 8 probe rows identical to perl).  The eighth --
the FAILURE path -- crashes.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3; scratch/s492a/probes/m5-filecopy.pl row 08
in the s492a worktree):
  use File::Copy;
  print copy("/tmp/does-not-exist", "/tmp/e.txt") ? "ok" : "false";
  perl: false
  PCL:  Unhandled sb-int:compiled-program-error
        Form: (go :fail_open1)
        Compile-time error: attempt to GO to nonexistent tag: :fail_open1

File::Copy.pm uses perl's forward `goto LABEL` three times in one sub:
  148:  open $from_h, "<", $from or goto fail_open1;
  184:  close($from_h) || goto fail_open1 if $closefrom;
  204: fail_open1:
      return 0;

THE COMPILER EMITS BOTH LOWERINGS IN THE SAME SUB (read from
`./pl2cl --module .../File/Copy.pm`):
  line 303:  (progn (p-or (p-open $from_h "<" $from) (go :fail_open1))
  line 322:  (catch :pcl-goto-fail_open1
  line 372:  (p-|| (p-close $from_h) (throw :pcl-goto-fail_open1 nil))
so the site at 303 uses a `go` to a tagbody tag that the catch/throw lowering
never establishes.  The `catch` form is the one that works; the `go` is a
second reading of the same construct that was not converted with it
(CLAUDE.md rule 11: one construct, two lowerings, and they disagree).

WHY IT IS SILENT UNTIL IT IS NOT: the two `goto` sites differ in where they
sit -- one is inside the statement that opens the structure the label ends,
the other below it -- so a file can carry both and only fail when the FIRST
one is taken, which here means only when the source file cannot be opened.

WHY IT MATTERS: File::Copy is core and on the README's module list; its
error path is what every `copy(...) or die ...` takes.  `goto LABEL` is also
what several other core modules use for their unwinding.

BAR: an emission change in the goto lowering => corpus-diff (every differing
file explained), full sweep, guard rows (the two-site shape above in a small
sub, with perl as the oracle), inverse-verified.  `docs/ir-spec.md` 6.4 is
the section that describes goto and must say which lowering is THE one.
subject: A forward `goto LABEL` is lowered TWO ways in one sub -- `(go :LABEL)` with no enclosing tagbody beside the `catch`/`throw` form -- so core File::Copy's error path dies "attempt to GO to nonexistent tag"
